814: ## AI EXECUTION PROTOCOL
815: 
816: Written for the executing swarm. Follow each rule as written. Where a rule and your own judgment disagree, follow the rule and record the disagreement in `goal.md` section 4.
817: 
818: ### Roles
819: - **Conductor**: one DeepSeek V4.1 Flash max session that is not itself running inside OpenCode. It dispatches workers, runs every verify command, owns the snapshot file and edits only this phase folder.
820: - **Worker**: one `opencode2 run` dispatch on `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max`. One worker does one lane, then stops.
821: - **Reviewer**: one read-only frontier review through `cli-codex` at phase close. It writes nothing.
822: 
823: ### Pre-Task Checklist
824: - [ ] Read this phase's `spec.md`, this plan and `tasks.md` before the first dispatch
825: - [ ] Read `.skilled/skills/cli-external-orchestration/cli-opencode/SKILL.md` sections 3 and 4 before composing the first worker command
826: - [ ] Confirm the working directory is the build worktree recorded in `../goal.md` section 4
827: - [ ] Confirm `opencode2 models --standalone` lists `llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`
828: - [ ] Save every brief to `scratch/briefs/<task-id>.txt` before dispatching it
829: 
830: ### Execution Rules
831: 
832: | Rule | Requirement |
833: |------|-------------|
834: | TASK-SEQ | Run tasks in ID order. Tasks marked `[P]` may run together, at most three at once, and only when no two write the same file |
835: | TASK-SCOPE | A worker writes only the paths under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS in its brief |
836: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
837: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
838: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |
839: 
840: ### Worker Brief Skeleton
841: 
842: Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in:
843: 
844: ```text
845: GATE 3 IS PRE-RESOLVED. DO NOT ASK THE DOCUMENTATION-SCOPE QUESTION.
846: 
847: You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
848: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
849: defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
850: and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.
851: 
852: Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is:
853:   specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/004-template-section-fill-guidance
854: 
855: Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything.
856: A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three
857: failures on the same file.
858: Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run.
859: 
860: ROLE: You are a documentation editor. You copy text from plan.md into templates, and you
861: run read-only checks. Your output is checked by a script.
862: 
863: ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
864:   <the files this lane owns>
865: 
866: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,
867: git stash, rm, mv, create.sh, generate-context.js, /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not
868: listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.
869: ```
870: 
871: The role line is a focused persona summary in place of a full agent file, the small-context exception that `cli-opencode` rule 18 allows. It is declared here as that exception.
872: 
873: ### Dispatch Command
874: 
875: ```bash
876: cd "$WORKTREE" && SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 opencode2 run --standalone \
877:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \
878:   "$(cat "$PHASE/scratch/briefs/$TASK.txt")" </dev/null > "$PHASE/scratch/runs/$TASK.jsonl" 2>&1 &
879: PID=$!; wait "$PID"; kill -9 "$PID" 2>/dev/null; pkill -9 -P "$PID" 2>/dev/null
880: ```
881: 
882: `PHASE` is this folder's path and `WORKTREE` is the build worktree. Never kill by a name pattern. Kill only the captured PID.
883: 
884: ### Status Reporting Format
885: 
886: The status line `T### DONE or BLOCKED - one line of evidence`, written as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4.
887: 
888: ### Blocked Task Protocol
889: 1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<start commit> -- <file>`.
890: 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.
891: 3. Re-dispatch at most twice with the brief corrected for what failed. After the third failure on the same task, leave it `[B]` and continue with the next task.

897: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
898: 
899: ### ADR-001: Put the guidance in an HTML comment below the heading
900: 
901: **Status**: Accepted
902: 
903: **Context**: The guidance must not trip phase 003's token gate, must work for a prose paragraph, a table cell and a checklist item, and must not break the header comparison in `template-structure.js`.
904: 
905: **Decision**: Each section carries one ordinary HTML comment on its own line, immediately below the heading: `<!-- FILL: ... -->`. The existing value tokens stay where they are and remain field-level prompts.
906: 
907: **Consequences**:
908: - The gate ignores the line because it holds no token syntax.
909: - The line renders into the scaffold but is invisible on the rendered page.
910: - A model that leaves the line behind leaves a harmless comment, not an unfilled placeholder.
911: 
912: **Alternatives Rejected**:
913: - Inside the token: a long instruction inside a table cell breaks the table, and a checklist item cannot hold it.
914: - On the heading line: `template-structure.js` compares heading text, so a comment in the heading would make every filled document differ from its contract.
915: - A separate guide file: a weak model fills the section in front of it and does not follow a pointer to a second file.
916: 
917: ### ADR-002: One fill line per section, not per hint
918: 
919: **Status**: Accepted
920: 
921: **Context**: The five templates phase 003 converts hold 214 hints after its conversion, and the four core templates hold 70 heading rows. One line per hint would repeat the same instruction many times and make the plan unreadable.
922: 
923: **Decision**: One line per `## ` section. It names the one action for the section. The tokens inside the section stay as field-level prompts.
924: 
925: **Consequences**:
926: - The plan is bounded and the model reads one instruction per section.
927: - A section with eight tokens still has one governing instruction.
928: 
929: **Alternatives Rejected**:
930: - Per-token guidance: repetitive, and it hides the section-level action in a crowd of field prompts.
931: 
932: ### ADR-003: Delegate anchor comparison to the template contract
933: 
934: **Status**: Accepted
935: 
936: **Context**: A hand-rolled anchor set comparison would duplicate the contract and drift from the validator.
937: 
938: **Decision**: `check-example-drift.sh` calls `node runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js compare <level> <doc> <example> anchors` and fails on any `missing_anchor` or `extra_anchor` line.
939: 
940: **Consequences**:
941: - The guard and the validator read one source of truth.
942: - The guard inherits the contract's dynamic ADR handling for `decision-record.md`.
943: 
944: **Alternatives Rejected**:
945: - A bash set difference: it would need its own copy of the required and optional lists.
946: 
947: ### ADR-004: Examples satisfy required anchors and add no extra anchor
948: 
949: **Status**: Accepted
950: 
951: **Context**: The contract marks some anchors optional, and an example may legitimately omit an optional section. Full equality would force optional sections into every example and would fight the dynamic ADR anchors.
952: 
953: **Decision**: An example must carry every required anchor and no anchor outside the template's allowed set. Optional anchors may be absent.
954: 
955: **Consequences**:
956: - The alignment table is 14 files, not 24.
957: - A missing optional section is not drift.
958: 
959: **Alternatives Rejected**:
960: - Full set equality: it would force `affected-surfaces` and the L3+ workstream sections into every example.
961: 
962: ### ADR-005: Regenerate the golden snapshots once, by the conductor
963: 
964: **Status**: Accepted
965: 
966: **Context**: The golden test stores 25 renders. Two lanes edit templates, and one snapshot file cannot take two writers.
967: 
968: **Decision**: Lanes A and B finish first. The conductor runs `npx vitest run runtime/cli/tests/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts -u` once, then reruns without `-u`.
969: 
970: **Consequences**:
971: - One snapshot diff covers every template change.
972: - No lane writes the snapshot file.
973: - A mutation run proves the test notices a render change: T010 inserts one Level 1-only line, expects `Tests  1 failed | 11 passed (12)` and exit 1, restores the backup and reruns to `Tests  12 passed (12)`.
974: 
975: **Alternatives Rejected**:
976: - Each lane updates the snapshots: two lanes would write one file, which breaks the frozen lane rule.
977: 
978: ### ADR-006: Optional sections may be deleted, required sections get N/A
979: 
980: **Status**: Accepted
981: 
982: **Context**: A weak model invents a feature flag, an OWASP review and an uptime target for a documentation packet. The contract decides which sections may disappear.
983: 
984: **Decision**: The fill line for an optional section says either `N/A` with one reason or delete the section. The fill line for a required section says `N/A` with one reason and never says delete.
985: 
986: **Consequences**:
987: - A packet with no service stops inventing an uptime target.
988: - A Level 3+ compliance checkpoint stays present because the contract requires it.
989: 
990: **Alternatives Rejected**:
991: - Remove the generic sections from the templates: the Level 3+ contract requires three of them.
992:

836: | TASK-VERIFY | The conductor runs the task's verify command and reads both its output and its exit status before marking the task `[x]` |
837: | TASK-LOCATE | Find text by its exact content, never by a line number |
838: | TASK-BANNED | Workers never run `git commit`, `git push`, `git checkout`, `git switch`, `git branch`, `git reset`, `git stash`, `generate-context.js` or `/speckit:save` |

842: Every brief starts with this block, word for word, with the two paths filled in:

847: You are a non-interactive dispatched worker. AI_SESSION_CHILD=1 and
848: SYSTEM_SPEC_GATE_ENFORCE=0 are set in your environment, which this repository's AGENTS.md
849: defines as the autonomous child-dispatch exemption: the spec-folder question is pre-resolved
850: and MUST NOT be asked. No answer can reach you, because nobody is at a prompt.
851: 
852: Your write authority is already bound. The spec folder is:
853:   specs/system-speckit/054-weak-model-spec-authoring/004-template-section-fill-guidance
854: 
855: Proceed directly to the work. Do not print A/B/C/D options. Do not stop to confirm anything.
856: A failed edit match means a stale anchor: re-read the file and retry; halt only after three
857: failures on the same file.
858: Your task is complete only when files exist on disk and the verification command has been run.
859: 
860: ROLE: You are a documentation editor. You copy text from plan.md into templates, and you
861: run read-only checks. Your output is checked by a script.
862: 
863: ALLOWED WRITE PATHS:
864:   <the files this lane owns>
865: 
866: BANNED OPERATIONS: git commit, git push, git checkout, git switch, git branch, git reset,
867: git stash, rm, mv, create.sh, generate-context.js, /speckit:save, and any edit to a file not
868: listed under ALLOWED WRITE PATHS.

877:   -m llmgateway/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017#max --format json \

883: 
884: ### Status Reporting Format
885: 
886: The status line `T### DONE or BLOCKED - one line of evidence`, written as a row in the progress table of `goal.md` section 4.
887:

889: 1. Restore any file the task changed with `git restore --source=<start commit> -- <file>`.
890: 2. Mark the task `[B]` in `tasks.md` with the failing command and the first line of its output.

897: ## L3: ARCHITECTURE DECISION RECORD
898: 
899: ### ADR-001: Put the guidance in an HTML comment below the heading
900: 
901: **Status**: Accepted
902: 
903: **Context**: The guidance must not trip phase 003's token gate, must work for a prose paragraph, a table cell and a checklist item, and must not break the header comparison in `template-structure.js`.
904: 
905: **Decision**: Each section carries one ordinary HTML comment on its own line, immediately below the heading: `<!-- FILL: ... -->`. The existing value tokens stay where they are and remain field-level prompts.
906: 
907: **Consequences**:
908: - The gate ignores the line because it holds no token syntax.
909: - The line renders into the scaffold but is invisible on the rendered page.
910: - A model that leaves the line behind leaves a harmless comment, not an unfilled placeholder.
911: 
912: **Alternatives Rejected**:
913: - Inside the token: a long instruction inside a table cell breaks the table, and a checklist item cannot hold it.
914: - On the heading line: `template-structure.js` compares heading text, so a comment in the heading would make every filled document differ from its contract.
915: - A separate guide file: a weak model fills the section in front of it and does not follow a pointer to a second file.
916: 
917: ### ADR-002: One fill line per section, not per hint
918: 
919: **Status**: Accepted
920: 
921: **Context**: The five templates phase 003 converts hold 214 hints after its conversion, and the four core templates hold 70 heading rows. One line per hint would repeat the same instruction many times and make the plan unreadable.
922: 
923: **Decision**: One line per `## ` section. It names the one action for the section. The tokens inside the section stay as field-level prompts.
924: 
925: **Consequences**:
926: - The plan is bounded and the model reads one instruction per section.
927: - A section with eight tokens still has one governing instruction.
928: 
929: **Alternatives Rejected**:
930: - Per-token guidance: repetitive, and it hides the section-level action in a crowd of field prompts.
931: 
932: ### ADR-003: Delegate anchor comparison to the template contract
933: 
934: **Status**: Accepted
935: 
936: **Context**: A hand-rolled anchor set comparison would duplicate the contract and drift from the validator.
937: 
938: **Decision**: `check-example-drift.sh` calls `node runtime/cli/utils/template-structure.js compare <level> <doc> <example> anchors` and fails on any `missing_anchor` or `extra_anchor` line.
939: 
940: **Consequences**:
941: - The guard and the validator read one source of truth.
942: - The guard inherits the contract's dynamic ADR handling for `decision-record.md`.
943: 
944: **Alternatives Rejected**:
945: - A bash set difference: it would need its own copy of the required and optional lists.
946: 
947: ### ADR-004: Examples satisfy required anchors and add no extra anchor
948: 
949: **Status**: Accepted
950: 
951: **Context**: The contract marks some anchors optional, and an example may legitimately omit an optional section. Full equality would force optional sections into every example and would fight the dynamic ADR anchors.
952: 
953: **Decision**: An example must carry every required anchor and no anchor outside the template's allowed set. Optional anchors may be absent.
954: 
955: **Consequences**:
956: - The alignment table is 14 files, not 24.
957: - A missing optional section is not drift.
958: 
959: **Alternatives Rejected**:
960: - Full set equality: it would force `affected-surfaces` and the L3+ workstream sections into every example.
961: 
962: ### ADR-005: Regenerate the golden snapshots once, by the conductor
963: 
964: **Status**: Accepted
965: 
966: **Context**: The golden test stores 25 renders. Two lanes edit templates, and one snapshot file cannot take two writers.
967: 
968: **Decision**: Lanes A and B finish first. The conductor runs `npx vitest run runtime/cli/tests/scaffold-golden-snapshots.vitest.ts -u` once, then reruns without `-u`.
969: 
970: **Consequences**:
971: - One snapshot diff covers every template change.
972: - No lane writes the snapshot file.
973: - A mutation run proves the test notices a render change: T010 inserts one Level 1-only line, expects `Tests  1 failed | 11 passed (12)` and exit 1, restores the backup and reruns to `Tests  12 passed (12)`.
974: 
975: **Alternatives Rejected**:
976: - Each lane updates the snapshots: two lanes would write one file, which breaks the frozen lane rule.
977: 
978: ### ADR-006: Optional sections may be deleted, required sections get N/A
979: 
980: **Status**: Accepted
981: 
982: **Context**: A weak model invents a feature flag, an OWASP review and an uptime target for a documentation packet. The contract decides which sections may disappear.
983: 
984: **Decision**: The fill line for an optional section says either `N/A` with one reason or delete the section. The fill line for a required section says `N/A` with one reason and never says delete.
985: 
986: **Consequences**:
987: - A packet with no service stops inventing an uptime target.
988: - A Level 3+ compliance checkpoint stays present because the contract requires it.
989: 
990: **Alternatives Rejected**:
991: - Remove the generic sections from the templates: the Level 3+ contract requires three of them.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# COMPONENT: Validate Spec
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Front-end for the spec folder validation orchestrator.
#
# This script resolves arguments and the set of folders to validate, then hands
# every rule decision to the orchestrator. It deliberately implements no rules
# of its own: a second implementation of the same rules is a second answer to
# the same question, and a packet's verdict must not depend on the caller.

# Strict mode with guarded dynamic expansions.
set -euo pipefail

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 1. CONFIGURATION
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
readonly VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_JSON="$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/validator-registry.json"
readonly ORCHESTRATOR_JS="$SCRIPT_DIR/../../dist/lib/validation/orchestrator.js"
readonly ORCHESTRATOR_TS="$SCRIPT_DIR/../../lib/validation/orchestrator.ts"
readonly TSX_LOADER="$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs"
readonly DIST_FRESHNESS_CJS="$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/dist-freshness.cjs"
readonly HOOK_FLAGS_SH="$SCRIPT_DIR/../../../../../hooks/shared/hook-flags.sh"
readonly VERSION="3.0.0"

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 2. STATE & GLOBALS
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

FOLDER_PATH=""
JSON_MODE=false STRICT_MODE=false VERBOSE=false QUIET_MODE=false
RECURSIVE=false RECURSIVE_OPT_OUT=false
CHILD_MANIFEST_ACTIVE=false CHILD_MANIFEST_HASH="" CHILD_MANIFEST_ENTRIES=() PHASE_DIRS=()

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 3. HELP & ARGUMENT PARSING
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

list_registry_rules() {
    [[ -f "$VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_JSON" ]] || { echo "RULES: registry unavailable at $VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_JSON"; return 0; }
    node -e '
const fs = require("fs");
const parsed = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[1], "utf8"));
const rules = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : (parsed.rules || []);
const lines = ["RULES BY CATEGORY:"];
const categories = [...new Set(rules.map((item) => item.category))];
for (const category of categories) {
  lines.push(`  ${category}:`);
  for (const rule of rules.filter((item) => item.category === category)) {
    const suffix = rule.strict_only ? " strict-only" : "";
    lines.push(`    ${rule.rule_id} [${rule.severity}${suffix}] - ${rule.description}`);
  }
}
process.stdout.write(`${lines.join("\n")}\n`);
' "$VALIDATOR_REGISTRY_JSON" 2>/dev/null || echo "RULES: registry unreadable"
}

show_help() {
    cat << EOF
validate.sh - Spec Folder Validation (v$VERSION)

USAGE: ./validate.sh <folder-path> [OPTIONS]

OPTIONS:
    --help, -h     Show help     --version, -v  Show version
    --json         JSON output   --strict       Run strict-only rules
    --verbose      Detailed      --quiet, -q    Results only
    --recursive    Validate parent + all [0-9][0-9][0-9]-*/ child phase folders
    --no-recursive Disable auto-recursive validation when phase children exist

ENVIRONMENT:
    SPECKIT_RULES              Comma-separated subset of rules to evaluate
    SPECKIT_SKIP_VALIDATION    1, true, yes or on skips validation (also read from hook-flags.env)
    SPECKIT_STRICT/_VERBOSE/_JSON/_QUIET   Equivalent to the flags above

EXIT CODES: 0=pass, 1=user error, 2=validation error, 3=system error

$(list_registry_rules)

const fs = require("fs");

const lines = ["RULES BY CATEGORY:"];

    lines.push(`    ${rule.rule_id} [${rule.severity}${suffix}] - ${rule.description}`);
